cards.title: Chinese Open-Weight Models Now Dominate: A Congressional Briefing on U.S.-China AI Competition
cards.why_it_matters: This is a field-level state-of-the-union on open-weight models that directly benchmarks the landscape you work in — including which labs and models are leading, and by how much.
cards.summary: Since ~April 2025, Chinese open-weight models have led American counterparts on capability benchmarks and Hugging Face downloads. As of September 2026, China's download lead stands at ~1.6B out of 3.2B total. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, top Chinese models (GLM-5.3: 45, Kimi K3: 44, GLM-5.3-Flash: 42) substantially outscore leading American open-weight models (Thinking Machines' Inkling: 26, Nvidia Nemotron 3 Ultra: 23).

cards.title: GameHorizon Suite: 5,000-Hour AAA Gameplay Dataset and Multi-Horizon Benchmark Across 47 Models
cards.why_it_matters: A large-scale, reproducible agent evaluation suite spanning visual understanding, planning, and action control is directly relevant to your interest in agents and evals.
cards.summary: GameHorizon Suite comprises an automated annotation pipeline, a dataset of 5,000 hours of gameplay from 21 AAA titles collected by 100 expert players with temporally aligned actions and multi-horizon instructions, and a benchmark with offline (standardized QA) and online (stepwise) evaluation tracks. Evaluating 47 models via over one million invocations, it reveals a clear hierarchy of task difficulty and significant model capability differences.

cards.title: Critical-State RL: Targeting Only Trainable States in Multi-Turn Tool Use Yields +14pp on BFCL
cards.why_it_matters: Identifying which turns in a multi-turn agent trajectory actually benefit from RL training is a core open problem — this method offers a principled diagnostic with strong empirical results.
cards.summary: Critical-State RL diagnoses which states in multi-turn tool-use interactions are 'trainable' by separating action-dependent reward variation from downstream continuation noise via nested sampling, then applies contextual-bandit training only at selected states. On BFCL v4, the method improves missing-function task performance by ~14 percentage points; training at non-selected states leaves performance flat or worse.

cards.title: WorldCrafter: Implicit 3D-Aware Memory Enables Long-Horizon Consistent Video World Models
cards.why_it_matters: World models with persistent, viewpoint-consistent memory are a key frontier for embodied agents and interactive simulation — this is a direct technical advance on that problem.
cards.summary: WorldCrafter introduces a camera-queryable implicit 3D-aware memory module trained jointly with a video diffusion generator. A pose-conditioned readout compresses multi-view historical observations into target-view-specific tokens before denoising, without explicit depth correspondences. Combined with recent temporal context and few-step distillation, it enables streaming scene exploration from a single image or text prompt, showing substantial gains in long-horizon consistency and camera-control accuracy over baselines.

cards.title: onPanda: Token-Level Correction Tool Cuts LLM Alignment Annotation Time by 52%
cards.why_it_matters: Efficient on-policy data collection is a practical bottleneck for RLHF/SFT pipelines — this tool and its annotation efficiency result are directly actionable for post-training workflows.
cards.summary: onPanda is an annotation tool where annotators identify the first inappropriate token in a model response, substitute it, and let the model continue from the corrected prefix, iterating until satisfactory. A controlled study reports 52% reduction in median annotation time versus manual post-editing. The resulting data preserves the model's sampling distribution for on-policy SFT and preference learning, and token-level corrections provide naturally paired positive-negative samples. A dataset (Panda-CVL) and benchmark are released.

cards.title: DexTacWAM: Tactile World-Action Model Averages 70.6 vs. 38.0 Baseline Across Six Dexterous Tasks
cards.why_it_matters: Integrating tactile sensing into video-based world models is a frontier problem for robotics and embodied AI — this result shows a data-efficient path from vision priors to contact-rich manipulation.
cards.summary: DexTacWAM injects per-fingertip tactile encodings through a finger- and pose-aware compressor into a video diffusion world model, enabling joint visuo-tactile world modeling. On six contact-rich tasks on a 22-DoF bimanual platform, it averages 70.6 vs. 38.0 for the strongest baseline. Ablations show removing tactile world modeling drops the four-task mean from 74.7 to 26.6. Tactile adaptation requires ~100 demonstrations per task after four hours of encoder fine-tuning, retaining visual quality within 0.5 dB of vision-only baselines.

cards.title: Block Pruning as Ising Glass: Physics-Based CBO Achieves +23pp MMLU at 50% Compression of Llama-70B
cards.why_it_matters: This is a technically deep result connecting statistical physics to LLM compression, directly relevant if you work on efficient inference or model deployment at scale.
cards.summary: Multiverse Computing reformulates transformer block removal as a constrained binary optimization (CBO) problem isomorphic to an Ising spin glass, capturing pairwise block-interaction couplings via a second-order Taylor expansion of the loss. The Ising energy serves as a cheap proxy for benchmark quality, enabling large-scale candidate ranking without benchmarking. At 50% compression of Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, the method gains ~23 percentage points on MMLU over the best competing block-removal method.

cards.title: Quantum Mpemba Effect Engineered via Stark Localization: Hotter States Cool Super-Exponentially Faster
cards.why_it_matters: A concrete quantum phenomenon with experimentally accessible signatures and a designed mechanism — relevant if you track frontier quantum computing results.
cards.summary: Researchers show that Stark localization can engineer a quantum energy landscape where local dissipation produces a Mpemba effect: hotter initial states cool faster than colder ones. The cooling rates for localized initial states are super-exponentially separated. The effect is further enhanced by collective hopping of bound pairs under attractive on-site interactions. The authors claim clear experimental signatures in present-day setups.

cards.title: Hugging Face tokenizers v1: Up to 10x+ Faster Encode/Decode via BPE and Pipeline Rewrites
cards.why_it_matters: Tokenizer throughput can bottleneck large-scale training and high-concurrency serving pipelines — this release directly affects your infrastructure stack.
cards.summary: tokenizers v1 preserves identical token IDs and API compatibility with v0.23 while substantially improving throughput, often by tens of times in benchmarks. Key changes include replacing regex-based pre-tokenization with hand-written bitstream splitters for fixed model patterns, plus stage-by-stage pipeline optimizations. Benchmarks cover single- and multi-threaded scaling, per-model/language performance, latency, decoding throughput, and memory usage. IBM, NVIDIA, and the ExecuTorch team contributed patches.
